candidate.educational_objective: Use aseptic technique and sterile equipment when inserting an indwelling urinary catheter in acute care.

options.A: Clean nonsterile technique with reusable lubricant
options.C: Sterile gloves only; the remaining insertion supplies may be nonsterile
options.D: No specific aseptic technique if the catheter will be removed within 24 hours

candidate.rationale: CDC CAUTI guidance states that in acute-care hospitals, urinary catheters should be inserted using aseptic technique and sterile equipment. Recommended supplies include sterile gloves, drape, sponges, an appropriate antiseptic or sterile solution for periurethral cleaning, and a single-use lubricant packet.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In acute-care hospitals, urinary catheters should be inserted using aseptic technique and sterile equipment, including sterile gloves, drape, sponges, appropriate cleansing solution, and single-use lubricant.
candidate.source_document_title: Guideline for Prevention of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections — Summary of Recommendations
candidate.source_locator: Section II Proper Techniques for Urinary Catheter Insertion, Recommendations II.C and II.C.1
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.source_version_date: 2009 guideline with CDC updates; current summary accessed 2026
candidate.stem: A nurse is inserting an indwelling urinary catheter in an acute-care hospital. Which technique is required?
